exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 What Does Success Mean?
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: Tom, do you think a person is successful only if they are rich and famous?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Not really. I think success means doing something you love and doing it well.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: So money is not the most important thing to you?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No. For me, a happy family and a job I enjoy matter more than money.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: That makes sense. My uncle is a village nurse, not rich at all, but he feels successful.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Exactly. He helps others every day, and that is a kind of success too.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: I agree. Maybe success is different for each person.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes, and the most important thing is to find your own road to it.

exercises.translation_cn: Lucy 问 Tom 是否只有又富又有名才算成功;Tom 认为成功是做自己热爱并做得好的事;对他来说幸福的家庭和喜欢的工作比金钱更重要;Lucy 提到当乡村护士的叔叔虽不富有却觉得成功;两人一致认为成功因人而异,最重要的是找到自己通向成功的路。

questions.stem: What does Tom think success mainly means?
options: Doing something you love and doing it well.

questions.stem: What matters more to Tom than money?
options: A happy family and a job he enjoys.

questions.stem: Why does Lucy mention her uncle?
options: Because he feels successful by helping others, though not rich.
Because he is famous on TV.
Because he wants a new job.

questions.stem: What do Lucy and Tom finally agree on?
options: Success can be different for each person.
Success is the same for everyone.

questions.stem: What does Tom say is the most important thing?
options: To give up when it is hard.
To find your own road to success.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 The Power of Grit
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Many people believe that talent is the key to success.
But studies show that something called grit matters even more.
A person with grit keeps working towards a goal for years, not just for days.
They treat life like a long marathon rather than a short race.
In the end, the habit of never giving up often decides who succeeds.
exercises.translation_cn: 许多人认为天赋是成功的关键;但研究表明一种叫'毅力'的品质更重要;有毅力的人会朝目标坚持数年,而非几天;他们把人生当作长跑而非短跑;最终,永不放弃的习惯常常决定谁能成功。

questions.stem: What do many people believe is the key to success?
According to studies, what matters even more?
How long does a person with grit keep working towards a goal?
What does a person with grit treat life like?
What often decides who succeeds in the end?
options: The habit of never giving up.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Cheer Up, You Can Do It
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: I'm so nervous about the maths competition tomorrow. I might fail.

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Don't worry too much. You have practised hard for weeks.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: But what if I forget everything in front of the judges?

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Take a few deep breaths before you start. That always calms me down.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Do you really think I have a chance?

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Of course. Even great people felt afraid before big moments.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Thanks, Jack. You always know how to cheer me up.

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Just do your best. Whatever happens, you should be proud of trying.

exercises.translation_cn: Mia 为明天的数学竞赛紧张,担心会失败;Jack 安慰说她已苦练数周;Mia 怕在评委面前忘光;Jack 建议开始前深呼吸几次来让自己镇定;并说连了不起的人在重要时刻前也会害怕;Mia 感谢 Jack 让她振作;Jack 让她尽力,无论结果如何都该为尝试而自豪。

questions.stem: Why is Mia nervous?
options: Because of a maths competition tomorrow.

questions.stem: What does Jack remind Mia she has done?
options: She has practised hard for weeks.

questions.stem: What does Jack suggest doing before she starts?
What does Jack say about great people?
options: They also felt afraid before big moments.

questions.stem: What does Jack tell Mia at the end?
options: To do her best and be proud of trying.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Never Give Up
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Almost every great achievement comes after many failures.
The first try is often the hardest, and many people stop too soon.
But those who keep going slowly learn from their mistakes.
Each failure teaches them something new and brings them closer to the goal.
So when you fail, do not lose heart; instead, start over and try again.
exercises.translation_cn: 几乎每一项伟大成就都来自多次失败;第一次尝试往往最难,许多人太早放弃;但坚持下去的人会慢慢从错误中学习;每一次失败都教会他们新东西,使他们更接近目标;所以当你失败时,别灰心,要重新开始再试一次。

questions.stem: What does almost every great achievement come after?
What do many people do too soon?
What do those who keep going learn from?
What does each failure do, according to the passage?
options: It teaches something new and brings you closer to the goal.

questions.stem: What should you do when you fail?

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Tips for a Good Speech
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Anna, you always give such great talks. How do you do it?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks! First, I write my main points on small cards.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Just the main points, not every word?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right. If you read every word, the talk sounds boring.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: What else helps you?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I practise out loud many times, and I pause at full stops and commas.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: That's clever. Anything for the nerves?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. Breathe slowly before you start, and speak to one friendly face at a time.

exercises.translation_cn: Ben 问 Anna 演讲为何总那么棒;Anna 说先把要点写在小卡片上;只写要点而非逐字;因为逐字读会很无聊;还会大声练习多次,并在句号逗号处停顿;对付紧张则是开始前慢慢呼吸,每次只对一张友善的面孔讲。

questions.stem: What does Anna write on her cards?
Why shouldn't you read every word?
Where does Anna pause when she speaks?
How does Anna deal with nerves?
Who does Anna suggest speaking to at a time?
options: The whole crowd at once with eyes shut.
One friendly face at a time.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 A Little Every Day
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: You do not have to do something huge to move towards success.
A small step taken every day adds up over time.
If you learn five new words a day, that is almost two thousand in a year.
The secret is not speed, but doing a little, again and again.
Be patient, keep going, and one day you will be surprised how far you have come.
exercises.translation_cn: 你不必做什么惊天动地的大事才能走向成功;每天迈出一小步,日积月累会很可观;如果每天学五个新词,一年就近两千个;秘诀不在快,而在一点一点反复地做;要有耐心,坚持下去,有一天你会惊讶自己走了这么远。

questions.stem: What does the passage say you do NOT have to do?
options: Do something huge to move towards success.

questions.stem: What adds up over time?
options: A small step taken every day.

questions.stem: If you learn five new words a day, how many is that in a year?
What is the secret, according to the passage?
options: Working only when you feel like it.
Doing a little, again and again.

questions.stem: What will happen if you keep going patiently?
options: One day you will be surprised how far you have come.
